transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-08
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (Apollo Head of Cloud Partnerships), Marcus Li (Platform Engineer), Evelyn Park (Security Architect)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for private deployments (VPC + peering pattern), and KMS compatibility for customer-managed keys. Decide pilot scope and next milestones.

Topics:
- Marketplace packaging checklist and listing artifacts
- Networking: VPC peering, CIDRs, NAT/egress, load balancer patterns
- Deployment topologies: hosted vs dedicated vs private (on-prem/VPC)
- KMS/HSM and encryption-at-rest and audit/logging expectations
- Pilot plan and validation tests (helm chart, operator, perf smoke test)

Action items (recap at top): see metadata section.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Kim: all right hello everyone thanks for joining, um feel free to say hi in the chat if you're coming in late. we have about 45 minutes, we'll try to cover the packaging checklist, and then priya will demo the helm pattern we suggest.
[00:28] Dana Ortiz: thanks alex, appreciate it. we just want to be sure listing in the marketplace won't require big architecture changes on our side. timeline is a bit compressed for our q2 launch.
[00:45] Alex Kim: totally, this is why we're doing this sync — aim is low-friction listing. priya, quick intro?
[00:54] Priya Sharma: hey all, priya here, SE on the integrations team. i'll walk through the chart pattern we recommend, plus the networking patterns (VPC peering and private link). note: some of the names from our auto notes may be off — "redwoodn" in the doc, lol.
[01:18] Marcus Li: haha noted. our infra is mostly k8s on managed nodes, we run a NAT + egress gateway, and we have strict outbound rules — so curious about egress requirements.
[01:34] Priya Sharma: perfect — for the marketplace listing we support both a shared hosted runtime option and a private deployment. for private, we usually recommend two patterns: 1) VPC peering with customer-managed subnets and customer-provided KMS; 2) connector-based private link for customers who don't want peering. either way, minimal routes are needed, and we'll provide a guide.
[02:02] Evelyn Park: on KMS — we have to ensure HSM-backed keys for certain PII workflows. how mature is your KMS integration? is there a way to bring our own HSM?
[02:18] Priya Sharma: yes we have a BYOK flow — we support customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS providers and there is an on-prem HSM option for private deployments. we'll share a doc with the exact key wrapping and envelope encryption steps.
[02:34] Dana Ortiz: do you have a SOC2 report? our procurement requires it for listing on our internal marketplace catalog.
[02:42] Alex Kim: we do; i'll share the SOC2 summary and the security package after this call. link will be in the follow-up note.
[02:50] Marcus Li: on networking, port whitelist? load balancer? do we need static IPs?
[03:00] Priya Sharma: for the peering pattern you won't need static outbound IPs for model traffic — but for webhook callbacks or license callbacks we recommend either NAT with static egress or a small set of whitelisted endpoints. we'll capture those endpoints in the checklist.
[03:22] Alex Kim: quick question — are you planning to use our hosted inference for the pilot or go straight to private?
[03:29] Dana Ortiz: pilot hosted would be simplest but we have strict data rules for prod, so likely private for production. need to validate perf first though.
[03:40] Priya Sharma: makes sense. we can do a hosted pilot to validate func and then migrate to dedicated/private. the packaging for marketplace is the same but we add a "private deployment" tag and a config snippet.
[04:00] Marcus Li: perf — do you have benchmark sheets for typical LLM sizes? we want tail latency numbers at 8k and 16k token workloads.
[04:12] Alex Kim: yes, we have a benchmark spreadsheet and we can run a short smoke perf test during pilot. i'll include the spreadsheet link; priya can recommend model variants and quantization profiles.
[04:30] Priya Sharma: for long context we usually recommend a 4-bit quantized variant for cost but if you need low-latency at 16k tokens we often suggest the fp16 variant on dedicated GPUs. it's a tradeoff — we'll lay out expected p95 and tokens/sec in the doc.
[05:02] Evelyn Park: audit logs — we need immutable audit trails for admin actions and who accessed the inference logs. is that in the product?
[05:12] Priya Sharma: yes logging and audit trails are part of our platform. with private deployments you can forward logs to your SIEM (we support syslog/JSON export) and the control plane has RBAC and SSO support.
[05:30] Dana Ortiz: timeline — can you outline the pilot phases? we need dates to present to internal stakeholders.
[05:38] Alex Kim: sure — phase 1: packaging + security review (2 weeks), phase 2: hosted pilot perf run (1 week), phase 3: private deployment dry-run (2–3 weeks), phase 4: production rollout. we'll propose exact dates in the note.
[06:00] Marcus Li: on the deployment template — do you provide a helm chart or an operator?
[06:07] Priya Sharma: we publish a helm chart and an optional operator for lifecycle management. for marketplace listing we recommend providing a packaged helm chart and a sample values.yaml; we'll include a small wrapper in the listing to allow "one-click" deploy on supported clusters.
[06:30] Alex Kim: i'm going to drop the packaging checklist link in chat: https://drive.redwood.example/partners/apollo/packaging-checklist (note: placeholder)
[06:45] Marcus Li: perfect. i'll take a look after.
[06:52] Priya Sharma: ok demo time — i'll share my screen and show the helm chart flow. please bear with me if the recording captions are wonky, sometimes the auto-transcription mangles args.
[07:10] [screen share starts]
[07:20] Priya Sharma: so this is our chart, top level has values for "deployment.mode" which can be hosted|dedicated|private. for private you'll see networking.vpcPeer and kms.provider keys.
[07:40] Marcus Li: can you show the section for proxy/egress? we use an egress gateway.
[07:46] Priya Sharma: sure, network.egress.path allows a sidecar proxy option. there is a note: if you have strict egress rules you may need to set network.egress.staticIps to maintain callback stability.
[08:12] Evelyn Park: what's the default retention for user data / logs in hosted mode? i know some vendors keep tokens longer than needed.
[08:21] Priya Sharma: by default hosted retains logs for 30 days but you can configure retention and export to your own S3 or log archive. for private deployments retention is under your control.
[08:35] Dana Ortiz: any special cert requirements for mutual TLS between our infra and redwood connectors?
[08:42] Priya Sharma: we support mTLS; for private deployments we generally recommend mTLS with cert rotation — we have a cert playground you'll use in the onboarding repo.
[09:00] Alex Kim: switching gears — marketplace listing metadata: what do you need from Apollo? screenshots, one-page solution blurb, pricing model, contact info, support SLA.
[09:12] Dana Ortiz: screenshots and a partner blurb are fine, pricing TBD. support SLA we need to align — enterprise customers ask for 24x7 and runbooks.
[09:28] Alex Kim: we can offer optional enterprise support add-on for marketplace listings that includes 24x7, and we can surface support contacts on the listing.
[09:40] Marcus Li: two technical questions: 1) does the listing allow users to deploy to their own cloud account through the marketplace? 2) Any constraints on container images / ECR policies?
[09:53] Priya Sharma: yes, many marketplaces allow "deploy to customer's account" via a marketplace workflow — our chart is compatible. for images we support OCI-compliant images; we can provide a signed attestation if your security team needs it.
[10:14] Dana Ortiz: procurement will want to know about indemnities and data residency. we'll send legal contacts after this call.
[10:22] Alex Kim: noted — i'll loop in our legal and procurement counterparts.
[10:30] Marcus Li: when you said "connector-based private link" earlier — can you explain the difference between that and VPC peering?
[10:36] Priya Sharma: sure — VPC peering creates a direct route and is lower-latency for heavy throughput, but requires network-level peering and route management. connector/private-link uses an egress connector with TLS tunnels to our ingress; it avoids peering but has slightly higher latency; it's easier for customers who can't or won't do peering.
[11:05] Evelyn Park: for compliance, can we run an on-prem variant? some of our servers are air-gapped.
[11:12] Priya Sharma: yes we have an on-prem package that's essentially the same runtime but installs behind your firewall; that requires a separate licensing and support agreement. we can share the install steps in the repo.
[11:30] Dana Ortiz: ok good. pilot scope — what minimal acceptance criteria would you propose for us?
[11:37] Priya Sharma: i'd say: 1) successful helm deploy in dev, 2) smoke inference test with sample prompt suite (quality within expected range), 3) p95 latency under agreed threshold on hosted pilot, 4) successful data plane connectivity for private. those are small and measurable.
[12:00] Marcus Li: on the smoke test, can you provide the prompt set and scoring script?
[12:06] Priya Sharma: yep — we'll attach a prompt set and scoring harness in the pilot artifacts.
[12:18] Alex Kim: putting a tentative schedule: packaging + checklist by 2/11, hosted pilot run 2/14–2/18, private deployment dry run 2/21–3/04. we'll confirm in the follow-up.
[12:35] Dana Ortiz: sounds reasonable, i'll try to get internal sign-off for those dates.
[12:44] Marcus Li: small nit — the helm chart references "k8s 1.27+" — our clusters are 1.26. how strict is that?
[12:52] Priya Sharma: the chart has optional APIs; we can backport a compatibility patch for 1.26 quickly. i'll note that as an action.
[13:10] Alex Kim: (typing) noted: compatibility patch for 1.26.
[13:18] [14:00-36:00 — technical deep dive continued, omitted timestamps for brevity in auto-notes; highlights below]
[14:00] Priya Sharma: demo continued — lifecycle hooks, canary deploy flags in values, and a builtin fallback to a smaller model variant if latency spikes.
[15:15] Marcus Li: interesting — fallback behavior: is that client-side or server-side? we need determinism across requests.
[15:25] Priya Sharma: server-side, policy-driven. you can set a hard latency SLO and we route to a compatible smaller model variant automatically. it's documented in the rollout policy doc.
[16:10] Evelyn Park: audit trail question again — are admin actions logged with user identity from SSO?
[16:18] Priya Sharma: yes, admin actions are tied to your SSO identity and exported in the audit log stream.
[17:05] Dana Ortiz: any rate limiting concerns if we have spikes from internal users during UAT?
[17:12] Alex Kim: we have token-level rate limiting and per-tenant quotas; for pilots we can raise quotas or add burst capacity on dedicated pools.
[18:00] Marcus Li: about cost metrics — can we see per-route token-level cost estimates before a big rollout?
[18:08] Priya Sharma: yes, the console shows token breakdown and cost estimators per model and route. we'll give you a read-only view for the pilot.
[19:00] Dana Ortiz: great. also, can we white-label the UX for our internal users?
[19:07] Alex Kim: we offer configurable branding on the console for enterprise plans; we'll include options in the partner listing details.
[20:00] Marcus Li: demo wrap — i like the fallback policy.
[20:08] Priya Sharma: ok quick recap and next steps. i'll list the artifacts: packaging checklist (drive link), helm chart repo (git link), pilot harness (perf and prompt set), SOC2 summary and security packet. i'll put links in the follow-up.
[20:30] Dana Ortiz: thanks — any blockers from our side? we need to confirm legal and procurement timelines.
[20:38] Alex Kim: i'll coordinate legal intro.
[20:44] Dana Ortiz: one more — our enterprise customers require egress IP allowlisting for callbacks. can you provide an IP list?
[20:53] Priya Sharma: for hosted we have a small set of egress IPs for callbacks, yes. for private it's under your control. i'll include the list.
[21:10] Marcus Li: ok i think that's everything.
[21:15] Alex Kim: cool — recapping action items, we'll send the packaging checklist, the SOC2 packet, and priya will run helm tests. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the next three business days.
[21:30] Dana Ortiz: thanks all.
[21:36] [call ends]

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few proper noun errors (Redwood sometimes captured as "redwoodn" or "read wood") and some boilerplate from the screen share was garbled.
